security_audit.summary: All 94 static findings were adjudicated as false positives. Most matches are Markdown syntax, documentation references, changelog text, SVG path data, or bundled Mermaid code; no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior was found in the reviewed material.

remediation.issue: The repository bundles a large minified Mermaid asset that exceeds the static scanner limit.
remediation.suggestion: Document the upstream version and integrity source for the bundled Mermaid file, or load it through a reproducible dependency process.

remediation.issue: Documentation describes local files, SQLite access, background indexing, and an API-key requirement, which creates many scanner false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Keep these examples clearly scoped to local project data and state that API keys are optional and never logged or transmitted by the plugin.

content.value_statement: Large repositories make it hard to find symbols and retain useful context. This skill builds a local symbol index and exposes focused MCP queries for faster code exploration.
actual_capabilities: Indexes Python, Rust, and C++ symbols with language-aware parsers.
Searches functions, classes, methods, and other indexed symbols through MCP tools.
Retrieves indexed symbol content, signatures, docstrings, and locations.
Lists indexed files and reports repository indexing status.
Detects similar code patterns with fuzzy duplicate detection.
Maintains local project context through manifests, narratives, learnings, and goals.
limitations: Language-aware symbol indexing supports Python, Rust, and C++ only.
MCP queries require the repository index and server to be available.
Initial indexing can take time for very large repositories.
Symbol search does not replace text search for comments, strings, or configuration values.

use_cases.title: Navigate an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Find classes, functions, and definitions without broad text searches.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers joining an existing project

use_cases.title: Investigate a large codebase
use_cases.description: Use symbol queries to inspect signatures, source locations, and related code quickly.

use_cases.title: Preserve project context
use_cases.description: Maintain local manifests, learnings, narratives, and goals across long work sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Find a symbol
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the symbol named ConfigLoader and show its signature and location.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a file
prompt_templates.prompt: List the indexed symbols in src/utils.py and summarize each responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for symbols matching setup_*. Then show the source for the most relevant setup function.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository map to identify symbols affected by adding a Rust parser. Summarize dependencies and propose a change plan.

output: Signature and docstring identify its constructor and loading methods.
A focused list of functions and classes with signatures.
Source locations help select the next symbol to inspect.
Index status shows whether indexing is running, completed, or failed.
The result includes symbol count and the last indexed time when available.

best_practices: Use symbol search for code definitions and text search for comments, strings, and configuration values.
Wait for initial indexing to complete before relying on search results.
Use exact symbol names when retrieving source content to avoid ambiguity.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the symbol index as complete for unsupported languages.
Do not use symbol search as a replacement for reviewing runtime behavior.
Do not query local index data as if it contains remote repository updates.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The skill indexes Python, Rust, and C++ source files.

faq.question: When should I use symbol search?
faq.answer: Use it to find code definitions, signatures, and source locations.

faq.question: When should I use text search instead?
faq.answer: Use text search for comments, strings, configuration, and arbitrary text.

faq.question: Does indexing happen automatically?
faq.answer: The MCP server can start indexing on first use in a new codebase.

faq.question: Where is the symbol index stored?
faq.answer: The local repository index is stored under the project .claude directory.

faq.question: Does the skill support Codex?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
